question: Which GameSpy components, identifiers, and network paths does the version 1.3 image contain, how does the System Link game list reach a GameSpy LAN query, and which Internet discovery path does the title implement?

scope.gameSpyFunctions: Observed GameSpy SDK bodies between 0x82A07338 and 0x82A1B4A0; the band edges are not established.
scope.titleSessionLayer: Manager entry 0x82D8D170 on manager global 0x8314EFE0, factory 0x82CA28F0, GameSpy session table 0x82160348, XGI session table 0x82160450, and registry global 0x8314F204.
scope.boundary: Static inventory of components, identifier strings, title-to-SDK calls, the LAN query and QR2 host arguments, and the mode split between the two session tables. Runtime packets, delivery, join completion, NAT behavior, visible UI ownership of the System Link Refresh action, and the runtime values of the QR2 public and NAT-negotiation flags remain outside this packet.

The 8th register argument and the first stack argument are zero at this call and have no positional counterpart in the 14-parameter bbac5ff qr2_initA. runtimeObservation.source: One owner-operated 2026-10-12 System Link capture between two Xenia Canary Netplay instances, emulator SHA-256 5EBC1583E1DB5EE50FDA028461CAAF03CEE79D91B62FD0B1A3C9A08E1C67E8F9 (netplay_canary_experimental@b5f6f6ed6), running base default.xex SHA-256 B59B8957A3ED9DD90E9296C96D5C7AB1B16078D3F08B015582714A06C7D6A7BD with no title update, on two interfaces of one PC. Only structural facts were retained.
runtimeObservation.discovery: Every discovery datagram was addressed to 255.255.255.255. The client sent one 16-byte FE FD 02 echo to each port 26900 through 27000 (101 datagrams); host QR2 port 26900 answered with an 86-byte type 0x05 echo response, then the client sent a 23-byte FE FD 09 prequery and a 27-byte FE FD 00 query from a second OS-assigned port, answered with 15-byte and 201-byte replies. Each reply carries request bytes 3-6 at bytes 1-4.
runtimeObservation.differencesFromPin: Against UniSpySDK bbac5ff, the echo request is 16 bytes rather than 8, the echo response is 86 bytes, and replies and follow-up queries go to the limited broadcast address rather than to the sender.
runtimeObservation.join: Each instance opened one VDP (protocol 0xFE) socket on guest port 1000. Its datagrams carried a 2-byte big-endian length prefix, then GT2 magic FE FE; the handshake ran ClientChallenge, ServerChallenge, ClientResponse, Accept in 92 ms, and all play traffic used AppReliable and Ack on that port only.
runtimeObservation.negatives: Neither the capture nor either emulator log showed UDP to ports 53, 27900, or 27901, an XNetDnsLookup call, or XSessionSearch. That run sent no QR2 master heartbeat.
runtimeObservation.unboundSockets: The client's discovery sockets were never bound, so the host operating system chose the broadcast route; a lower-metric virtual adapter captured the first four sweeps until it was disabled.
runtimeObservation.qualification: This corroborates the mode-1 LAN query, QR2 host port, and GT2 join of the static result. It ran the base title version, not the pinned version 1.3 image, under Netplay's XNet emulation, whose broadcast and VDP handling is emulator behavior rather than console proof. It does not identify the runtime ispublic source or the UI owner of 0x82D6C398, and ReRevved was not run.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only Ghidra queries against the canonical version 1.3 project, a byte scan of the pinned flat image (SHA-256 5C7A8C3AD9B6A9D39CC9BBF3DA5AB23015A568C65C723D298F846086324C4680), exact-function generated-code reads, and comparison with the UniSpySDK pin and the maintained SDK XGI handler, with external emulator runtime corroboration in runtimeObservation.

entries.result: Gamename civconps3 and a six-byte immediate secret key populate registry +0x78 and +0x7C.
LAN-only QR2 browser and broadcast echo to UDP 26900 through 27000.
QR2 query socket on the first free UDP port from 26900 within 100 ports.
Mode 1 selects GameSpy LAN; other modes select XGI search.
Messages 0x000B0016 and 0x000B001B from the mode-2 table.
No title entry in direct, tail-branch, or pointer forms.
Xenia Netplay observed the QR2 limited-broadcast exchange on UDP 26900-27000, host QR2 port 26900, a GT2 join on guest port 1000, and no master traffic.

currentEvidence.qualification: Static control flow and arguments establish code paths and constants, not runtime delivery, the values of runtime flags, successful binds, or reply handling. The guest GameSpy SDK differs from the UniSpySDK pin in the qr2_initA parameter count and the LAN echo request, so source names outside the accepted Server Browsing equivalence rest on body shape, strings, and call order.

guards: Do not record or reproduce the secret key value.
Do not treat mode 1 as System Link or mode 2 as Xbox LIVE from UI labels alone; the split is proved by the session tables, not by visible strings.
Do not assume QR2 contacts the GameSpy master in System Link play; it depends on the runtime value at 0x82C9F438, and the one emulator run sent no master traffic.
Do not infer that the visible Refresh action reaches 0x82C9D978 from this static chain.
Do not treat the SDK XGI message labels as guest proof beyond the matching request sizes and fields.
Do not infer runtime discovery, reply parsing, join completion, NAT traversal, or Internet play from this static inventory.
conclusion: Version 1.3 embeds GameSpy QR2, Server Browsing, GT2, and an unreached availability check, and carries no NAT Negotiation, GP, GameStats, SAKE, Peer/Chat, CD-key, or MOTD host. Its gamename is the PlayStation 3 identifier civconps3, and a six-byte secret key is built from immediates in 0x82D8CC28. Session mode 1 installs table 0x82160348: browsing creates a LAN-only QR2 Server Browser and broadcasts a 16-byte QR2 echo to UDP ports 26900 through 27000, and hosting calls qr2_initA with base port 26900, binding the first free port up to 26999. Other modes install table 0x82160450, which searches through XGI messages 0x000B0016 and 0x000B001B and makes no GameSpy call. No title path reaches the GameSpy master list; a QR2 master heartbeat depends on a runtime flag. One emulator capture of the base title corroborated the mode-1 exchange, QR2 port 26900, a GT2 join on guest port 1000, and no master traffic. The visible Refresh action and the static source of the runtime flags remain unjoined.
